lines.text: This angle looks tiny. But a neat pattern is hiding here.
lines.caption: This angle looks tiny. But a neat pattern is hiding here.

lines.text: We only get ONE number to start with. Can we chase it all the way here?
lines.caption: We only get ONE number to start with. Can we chase it all the way here?

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's go angle chasing together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's go angle chasing together.

lines.text: Here's the question. Triangle A B C is equilateral.
lines.caption: Here's the question. Triangle A B C is equilateral.

lines.text: Point D is on side B C, and point E is on side A C.
lines.caption: Point D is on side B C, and point E is on side A C.

lines.text: The little tick marks say A D and A E are equal.
lines.caption: The little tick marks say A D and A E are equal.

lines.text: Angle B A D is twenty degrees.
lines.caption: Angle B A D is twenty degrees.

lines.text: What is x, the angle E D C?
lines.caption: What is x, the angle E D C?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we know? Equilateral means every angle is sixty degrees.
lines.caption: So what do we know? Equilateral means every angle is sixty degrees.

lines.text: A D equals A E, so triangle A D E has two equal sides.
lines.caption: A D equals A E, so triangle A D E has two equal sides.

lines.text: We want the small angle at D, between D E and side D C.
lines.caption: We want the small angle at D, between D E and side D C.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's start at the top corner, A.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's start at the top corner, A.

lines.text: The whole angle at A is sixty. Angle B A D takes twenty of it.
lines.caption: The whole angle at A is sixty. Angle B A D takes twenty of it.

lines.text: So angle D A E is sixty minus twenty. That's forty degrees.
lines.caption: So angle D A E is sixty minus twenty. That's forty degrees.

lines.text: Now look at triangle A D E. It's isosceles: two sides are equal.
lines.caption: Now look at triangle A D E. It's isosceles: two sides are equal.

lines.text: Side D E is the base. The angles at D and E, the base angles, are equal.
lines.caption: Side D E is the base. The angles at D and E, the base angles, are equal.

lines.text: Its three angles add up to one hundred eighty. Take away forty, and one hundred forty is left.
lines.caption: Its three angles add up to one hundred eighty. Take away forty, and one hundred forty is left.

lines.text: Split it in half. Each base angle is seventy degrees.
lines.caption: Split it in half. Each base angle is seventy degrees.

lines.text: Here's the clever step. Look at triangle A B D on the left.
lines.caption: Here's the clever step. Look at triangle A B D on the left.

lines.text: Angle A D C sits outside that triangle, on the straight line B C.
lines.caption: Angle A D C sits outside that triangle, on the straight line B C.

lines.text: An outside angle equals the two far inside angles added together.
lines.caption: An outside angle equals the two far inside angles added together.

lines.text: Why? Triangle A B D adds up to one hundred eighty. So does the straight line at D.
lines.caption: Why? Triangle A B D adds up to one hundred eighty. So does the straight line at D.

lines.text: Both include angle A D B, so the leftover parts must match.
lines.caption: Both include angle A D B, so the leftover parts must match.

lines.text: That's angle B, sixty, plus angle B A D, twenty. So angle A D C is eighty.
lines.caption: That's angle B, sixty, plus angle B A D, twenty. So angle A D C is eighty.

lines.text: Angle A D C is made of two parts: angle A D E, and our x.
lines.caption: Angle A D C is made of two parts: angle A D E, and our x.

lines.text: So x is eighty minus seventy.
lines.caption: So x is eighty minus seventy.

lines.text: That's ten degrees! The answer is A.
lines.caption: That's ten degrees! The answer is A.

scenes.chapter: Solution 2: the straight line at E

lines.text: Here's a second way. Angle A E D is seventy, and A E C is a straight line.
lines.caption: Here's a second way. Angle A E D is seventy, and A E C is a straight line.

lines.text: So angle D E C is one hundred eighty minus seventy. That's one hundred ten.
lines.caption: So angle D E C is one hundred eighty minus seventy. That's one hundred ten.

lines.text: Now look at the small triangle D E C. Angle C is sixty.
lines.caption: Now look at the small triangle D E C. Angle C is sixty.

lines.text: So x is one hundred eighty, minus one hundred ten, minus sixty. That's ten again!
lines.caption: So x is one hundred eighty, minus one hundred ten, minus sixty. That's ten again!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? It's a great double-check, using a straight line and the triangle sum.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? It's a great double-check, using a straight line and the triangle sum.

lines.text: Did you notice? Angle B A D was twenty, and x was ten. Exactly half!
lines.caption: Did you notice? Angle B A D was twenty, and x was ten. Exactly half!

lines.text: Is that luck? Let's call angle B A D the letter a, and redo our steps.
lines.caption: Is that luck? Let's call angle B A D the letter a, and redo our steps.

lines.text: Angle D A E is sixty minus a. So each base angle works out to sixty, plus half of a.
lines.caption: Angle D A E is sixty minus a. So each base angle works out to sixty, plus half of a.

lines.text: Angle A D C is sixty plus a. Subtract, and the two copies of sixty cancel.
lines.caption: Angle A D C is sixty plus a. Subtract, and the two copies of sixty cancel.

lines.text: So in this picture, x is ALWAYS half of angle B A D!
lines.caption: So in this picture, x is ALWAYS half of angle B A D!

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Twenty is angle B A D. That's the number we were given, not x.
lines.caption: Twenty is angle B A D. That's the number we were given, not x.

lines.text: Forty is angle D A E, at the top. It's not the angle at D.
lines.caption: Forty is angle D A E, at the top. It's not the angle at D.

lines.text: Thirty is what you would get if you used angle A D B instead.
lines.caption: Thirty is what you would get if you used angle A D B instead.

lines.text: Angle A D B is one hundred. One hundred minus seventy is thirty. But x is inside angle A D C, on the C side.
lines.caption: Angle A D B is one hundred. One hundred minus seventy is thirty. But x is inside angle A D C, on the C side.

lines.text: Fifteen is what you would get if A D cut angle A exactly in half. Then B A D is thirty, and half of thirty is fifteen. But ours is twenty.
lines.caption: Fifteen is what you would get if A D cut angle A exactly in half. Then B A D is thirty, and half of thirty is fifteen. But ours is twenty.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Mark every angle you find on the picture as you go.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Mark every angle you find on the picture as you go.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same picture, one new number.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same picture, one new number.

lines.text: Triangle A B C is still equilateral, and A D still equals A E.
lines.caption: Triangle A B C is still equilateral, and A D still equals A E.

lines.text: This time, angle B A D is thirty-six degrees. What is x?
lines.caption: This time, angle B A D is thirty-six degrees. What is x?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Angle D A E is sixty minus thirty-six. That's twenty-four.
lines.caption: Let's check. Angle D A E is sixty minus thirty-six. That's twenty-four.

lines.text: One hundred eighty minus twenty-four is one hundred fifty-six. Half is seventy-eight.
lines.caption: One hundred eighty minus twenty-four is one hundred fifty-six. Half is seventy-eight.

lines.text: Angle A D C is sixty plus thirty-six. That's ninety-six.
lines.caption: Angle A D C is sixty plus thirty-six. That's ninety-six.

lines.text: So x is ninety-six minus seventy-eight. That's eighteen degrees!
lines.caption: So x is ninety-six minus seventy-eight. That's eighteen degrees!

lines.text: And the pattern agrees. Half of thirty-six is eighteen.
lines.caption: And the pattern agrees. Half of thirty-six is eighteen.

lines.text: If you found eighteen, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found eighteen, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Find the angle at D with the outside angle trick.
lines.caption: Find the angle at D with the outside angle trick.

lines.text: Then take away the base angle of the isosceles triangle inside it.
lines.caption: Then take away the base angle of the isosceles triangle inside it.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep chasing those angles, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep chasing those angles, and I'll see you next time!
